holidays.name: National Marzipan Day
holidays.description: A sweet salute to the almond-and-sugar confection that gets molded into tiny fruits, animals, and cake toppings. Celebrate by nibbling marzipan, baking with it, or sculpting a questionable pig.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance popular on social media and in food calendars. Marzipan itself dates back centuries, with disputed origins in Persia, Spain, and Germany, and each region claims it as its own.
holidays.funFact: In Germany, marzipan pigs are given as good luck charms at New Year, and the city of Lübeck is famous for its marzipan, which it has produced since at least the 1800s.

holidays.name: National Curried Chicken Day
holidays.description: A day for savoring the warm, spicy, golden goodness of curried chicken, from Indian-style curries to Japanese curry and creamy coronation chicken.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday that appears on January 12 in many food-holiday calendars, created to celebrate the global popularity of curry dishes.
holidays.funFact: Coronation chicken, a cold curried chicken salad, was created for Queen Elizabeth II's coronation lunch in 1953.

holidays.name: Kiss a Ginger Day
holidays.description: A playful day dedicated to showing affection to redheads, who make up only about 1-2% of the world's population. Consent and good manners strongly recommended.
holidays.origin: A fun, unofficial observance that became popular online. The date is often listed as January 12 in quirky holiday calendars, though some lists place it on other dates.
holidays.funFact: Scotland has the highest percentage of redheads in the world, at roughly 13%, and about 40% of Scots carry the red-hair gene.

holidays.name: National Pharmacist Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the pharmacists who dispense medicine, catch dangerous drug interactions, and decipher doctors' handwriting like professional codebreakers.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States on January 12, as this day honors the vital role pharmacists play in healthcare and communities.
holidays.funFact: The word 'pharmacy' comes from the Greek 'pharmakon', which could mean medicine, poison, or magic charm, depending on context.
